title: Large restoration with bite and cold symptoms
scenario: A mandibular molar with a large MOD restoration; intermittent sharp pain on hard food and brief cold sensitivity; no spontaneous/nocturnal pain; negative percussion; no obvious periapical radiolucency. Cusp-specific bite testing, periodontal probing, and transillumination were not yet performed.
question: Explain your evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment plan.
authorOriginal: case 1- 먼저 환자에게 bite에 문제가 있는지 물어볼거 같아. 환자가 그게 무슨 말이냐고 물으면 그건 bite에 문제가 없는거니까 다음처럼 진행할꺼야. BU/CRN를 recommend 할거 같아. 지금 상황은 large restoration에 의한 기존 치아의 crack이 원인으로 보여져. 물론 보일수도 있고 안보일수도 있어. bite test에서 pain을 reproduce할수도 있고 하지 않을수도 잇어. crack이 root까지 이어졌다면 살릴수 없으니 ext/bone/implant가 맞고 지금은 최대한 빨리 bu/crn이 치아를 살릴수 있는 최고의 선택으로 보여. 환자가 bite force가 크거나 인지하든 인지하지 않든 night grind/clenching으로보고 night guard를 highly recommend 할거 같아. 만약에 환자가 bite에 문제가 있다고 하면 나는 다음에 이렇게 물어봐. jaw를 뒤로 보내거나 옆으로 보내야 bite을 맞출수 있냐고 물어보고 그렇다고 하면 그건 bite에 문제가 있는거니까 full mouth reconstruction을 고려할꺼야. bite에 문제가 있는건 jaw의 ideal position(Centric relation)과 teeth position의 discrepency가 존재하는거니까 kois deprogrammer로 먼저 한달간 jaw position을 이상적인 포지션이 되도록 훈련시키고 그 포지션에 맞게 치아를 세울꺼야. 그건 full mouth reconstruction case이기 때문에 치아 하나에 대해서 크라운을 진행하는게 아니라 치아 전체에 bite를 바꾸는 방법으로 진행할거고 그건 모든 치아에 대해 크라운을 씌워야 한다는 걸 의미해.
authorParaphrase:
1. Ask whether the patient has a problem with the bite.
2. In the stated approach, a patient asking what that means is interpreted as not recognizing a bite problem, and Dr. Chi proceeds toward single-tooth treatment.
3. Suspect a crack associated with the large restoration. The crack may not be visible, and bite testing may or may not reproduce pain.
4. Recommend timely BU/CRN with the intent of protecting the remaining tooth.
5. If the crack extends into the root, the original approach considers the tooth nonrestorable and favors extraction, bone grafting, and implant replacement.
6. With high loading concerns, suspect unrecognized nocturnal grinding/clenching and strongly recommend a night guard.
7. If the patient reports a bite problem, ask whether they must move the jaw backward or sideways to bring the teeth together.
8. A positive answer is interpreted in the original as a CR-to-tooth-position discrepancy.
9. The stated comprehensive pathway uses a Kois deprogrammer for approximately one month, then reconstructs the occlusion at the intended reference position. The original describes this as crowns on all teeth.

title: Symptoms after prior RCT
scenario: A crowned mandibular molar treated endodontically years earlier; intermittent chewing soreness and periapical radiolucency at one root; no swelling/sinus tract. Prior radiographs, occlusal exam, probing, crown-margin evaluation, and adjacent-tooth evaluation unavailable.
question: Explain your evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment plan.
authorOriginal: case 3- prognosis에 대해 설명할거 같아. RCT가 fail 한것으로 보인다. 그건 의사가 치료를 잘못해서라기 보다 워낙에 RCT 의 성공 확률은 높지 않다. 그래서 RCT보다는 ext/bone/implant를 추천하는 추세이다. 그런데 환자분이 살기길 원하면 RCT를 진행하지만 실패할수 잇음을 알리고 환자가 선택하도록 한다. 지금 상황에서는 option이 두가지다. 하나는 치료를 한 의사에게 돌아가서 재치료를 받는것이다. 여의치 않다면 전문의에게 가서 2nd opinion을 받는걸 추천한다. 치료가 가능하다면 치료를 받지만 재치료의 성공확률은 확연히 떨어지는걸 알아야 한다. fracture가 있거나 어떠한 이유에서든 재치료가 가능하지 않다면 우리에게 와서 ext/bone/implant을 진행해라. 성공확률은 높다. 97프로의 성공 확률이고 만약에 재치료과정을 겪기 싫으면 우리와 ext/bone/implant를 진행하면 된다. 실패 확률이 없지는 않는데 실패할 경우 다시 진행하면 된다. 크라운이 부러질수는 있지만 뿌리에 해당하는 임플란트는 한번 성공하면 계속 있는거다. 그건 나중에 뽑기가 더 어려운 상황이다. 어떤 치료를 받을지 선택하면 된다.

2. The stated counseling expresses concern about the reliability of RCT and especially retreatment and favors extraction/bone grafting/implant when appropriate.

5. If a fracture or other condition precludes retention, or the informed patient elects replacement, discuss extraction, bone grafting, and an implant.

title: Dry mouth and new root caries
scenario: A 67-year-old has three new root-surface caries lesions at #22, #27, and #28 over the past year, with gingival recession. The patient brushes three times daily and asks why new decay is developing.
findings: The patient reports dry mouth and waking at night for water.
Amitriptyline was started nine months ago.
Salivary flow, diet, fluoride exposure, the complete medication history, and lesion activity, depth, and restorability have not been assessed.
question: What would you assess first, and how would you explain your plan? Separate variation: if the lesions are active, other teeth have restorations, and most remaining teeth appear restorable with adequate periodontal support, what additional findings would move you toward considering All-on-X?
authorOriginal:
[CASE 017]
나도 Dr. B 와 같은 의견으로 먼저 dry mouth 부터 해결할거 같아. 전에도 말했듯이 root caries는 박테리아 수가 엄청 많다는 거고 caries risk가 크기 때문에 치료에 있어서도 크라운으로 치료하고 만약에 충치가 너무 깊으면 빼고 임플란트로 넘어갈꺼야. 이게 3개의 치아가 아니라 전체적인 문제라면 살릴려고 노력하기 보다는 오히려 all on X tx도 고려할꺼야. 지금 상황은 기존에 있는 크라운, filling 치료한 치아들도 recurrent decay의 위험이 상당히 높은 상황이야.

[CASE 017B]
더 많은 teeth가 영향을 받을때, 그리고 dry mouth가 개선이 안될때, 환자의 치아가 root caries로 인해 부러지기 시작할때.
authorParaphrase:
[CASE 017]
I agree with Doctor B and would address the dry mouth first. As I have said before, I interpret root caries as indicating a very high bacterial burden and high caries risk. Because of that risk, I would favor treatment with crowns; if the decay is too deep, I would move to extraction and implant replacement. If this is a generalized problem rather than one limited to three teeth, I would also consider All-on-X rather than trying to preserve the teeth. I would regard the existing crowned and filled teeth as being at substantial risk of recurrent decay.

[CASE 017B]
The factors that would move me toward considering All-on-X are more teeth becoming affected, dry mouth not improving, and teeth beginning to fracture because of root caries.

evidenceNotes: The separate clinical qualification distinguishes caries risk, tooth-specific restorability and full-arch prognosis. Crowns do not by themselves resolve underlying disease risk. Full-arch implant treatment also requires prevention and long-term maintenance. https://www.efp.org/for-patients/dental-implants/peri-implant-diseases/

title: Pain after wisdom-tooth extraction
scenario: Four days after extraction of #32, an adult reports worsening pain radiating toward the ear after initially feeling better. The patient requests antibiotics.
findings: No fever, increasing facial swelling, or difficulty swallowing is reported.
The socket and adjacent tissues have not been examined.
question: What would you examine first, and how would you explain your treatment plan?
authorOriginal: 사랑니후의 통증은 대부분 food trap 때문이야. saline으로 irrigate 하고 syringe를 줘서 식사후 그곳을 청소하라고 할거 같아. 그게 먼저고 그래도 infection 증후가 나타나면 그후에 antibiotic을 더 처방할거 같아. ext 후에 ibuprofen, amox를 주로 처방하고 impacted w. teeth 같은 경우는 decadron도 처방해. 임플란트를 심은 후에는 amox, T3 처방해. ibuprofen은 NSAIDS라 implant healing hinder가 될수 있거든.
authorParaphrase: I consider food trapping the cause of most pain after wisdom-tooth extraction. My first step would be saline irrigation and providing a syringe so the patient can clean the area after meals. If signs of infection subsequently appear, I would consider an additional antibiotic prescription. After extractions, I commonly prescribe ibuprofen and amoxicillin; for impacted wisdom teeth, I also prescribe Decadron. After implant placement, I prescribe amoxicillin and T3 because I am concerned that NSAIDs such as ibuprofen could interfere with implant healing.

title: My implant doesn't hurt. Why does it need treatment?
scenario:
A 61-year-old patient presents with occasional bleeding and a bad taste around implant #30.

"It doesn't hurt, and the implant isn't loose. Can you just clean it or give me antibiotics?"
findings: Implant placed and restored six years ago with a cement-retained crown.
No spontaneous pain.
Implant and crown are stable.
Probing depths: 7-8 mm, with bleeding and localized suppuration.
Comparable PAs show crestal bone loss increasing from approximately 1 mm to 4 mm over two years.
The crown contour makes interproximal cleaning difficult. Residual cement has not been assessed.
Smokes five cigarettes daily; most recent HbA1c: 8.0%.
Occlusion, implant position, defect morphology, and remaining circumferential bone support have not yet been evaluated.
question: What would you check first, and what findings would lead you to implant retention versus removal? Explain it as you would to the patient.
authorOriginal:
CASE 021 INITIAL RESPONSE
임플란트 심은지 1년내에 cretal bone loss가 일어나. 1년동안 1mm가 bone loss가 생겼으면 그후에 bone loss가 생길 확률은 극히 드물어. 그래서 너의 케이스는 현실적이지 않다라는 느낌이야. 다만 7mm의 probing depth가 생겼으면 임플란트가 stable하다 하더라도 infection이 계속 생기겠지. 내가 알기론 이런 경우 해결방법은 없어. 빼고 다시 심는수밖에는. 근데 환자가 결정할 일이야. 환자는 불편하지도 않고 사용하는데 문제가 없으면 그냥 상황을 지켜보는게 최선이야. 환자가 불편하다고 하면 의사가 불편해도 임플란트를 뽑는게 맞고. 이런 경우 해결 방법이 있는지 확인해봐.

CASE 021 POST-REVIEW AUTHOR POSITION
가상 환자에서는 implant removal가 맞네. 그리고 추가로 큰돈을 내면서 확실치 않은 치료를 할 환자는 없어보여. 그리고 보장도 안되고 다시 임플란트를 해야하는데 그 돈에 대해서도 새로 다 내야하면. 리스크 메니지먼트 차원에서 그렇게 좋은 치료가 아닌거 같아.
authorParaphrase:
Initial response:
"I expect crestal bone loss to occur within the first year after implant placement. If approximately 1 mm is lost during that year, I consider subsequent bone loss extremely rare, so this scenario feels unrealistic to me. However, with a 7 mm probing depth, I expect infection to recur even if the implant is stable. To my knowledge, there is no solution other than removal and replacement. The patient should decide. If there is no discomfort and the implant functions without difficulty, I consider observation the best approach. If the patient is uncomfortable, I favor removal even if that is uncomfortable for the clinician. Please check whether treatments are available for this situation."

Post-review position:
"In this fictional case, I consider implant removal the appropriate choice. I do not expect patients to pay substantial additional fees for treatment with uncertain results, particularly when there is no guarantee and they may later have to pay the full cost of another implant. From a risk-management perspective, reconstructive treatment does not seem like a favorable option here."

Source: https://www.efp.org/fileadmin/uploads/efp/Documents/Campaigns/New_Classification/Reports/Consensus_report__Workgroup_4__Berglundh_et_al-2018-Journal_of_Clinical_Periodontology.pdf

title: Do I really need a sinus lift?
scenario:
A 58-year-old patient requests a fixed replacement of #3, extracted two years ago.

"I want a fixed tooth, but I would prefer fewer surgeries and lower cost. Is a sinus lift necessary?"
findings: Healthy, nonsmoker; no diabetes or antiresorptive medication history.
CBCT: approximately 6-7 mm residual height from the crest to the sinus floor and approximately 8 mm width.
No sinus symptoms or obvious sinus pathology.
#2 and #4 already have crowns; no mobility; probing depths 2-3 mm.
Crown margins, underlying tooth structure and abutment prognosis still require evaluation.
Restorative space, opposing teeth, occlusion, parafunction and achievable primary stability have not been established.
question: What would you check first, and under what conditions would you select sinus augmentation, a short implant, or a bridge? Explain it as you would to the patient.
authorOriginal:
CASE 022 INITIAL RESPONSE
크라운을 잘 쓰고 잇는 상황에서 브릿지는 아닌거 같고 6-7mm height에 대해 vertical sinus lift를 진행할꺼야. 임플란트 심으면서 동시에 진행하기 때문에 환자 입장에서는 추가 수술이 아니고 통증도 없을꺼야.

CASE 022 AUTHOR CONTINGENCY ADDENDUM
그렇지.  implant placement를 미루지. 만약에 sinus lift가 성공하지 못해도 그냥 덮고 다음에 시도해. membrane perforate같은 경우.
authorParaphrase:
"Since the existing crowns are functioning well, I would not favor a bridge in this case. With 6-7 mm of residual bone height, I would perform a vertical sinus lift simultaneously with implant placement. From the patient's perspective, this would not involve a separate surgery, and I would expect no pain."

Contingency addendum:
"Yes. If adequate primary stability cannot be achieved, I would postpone implant placement. If I cannot successfully complete the sinus lift—for example, because of membrane perforation—I would close the site and attempt it again later."
